recommended_products.product: Debt Consolidation & Restructuring Facility (Refinancing of Existing Term Loans)
recommended_products.purpose: Refinance the two existing term loans (ICICI Bank TL INR 119 Mn + Aditya Birla Finance TL INR 52 Mn = INR 171 Mn outstanding) into a single longer-tenor amortising facility with a 6-month principal moratorium, reducing monthly EMI burden to a level EBITDA can service at DSCR ≥ 1.25
recommended_products.amount_basis: ICICI Bank TL outstanding INR 119,000,000 + Aditya Birla Finance TL outstanding INR 52,000,000 = INR 171,000,000 (conservative: uses outstanding balances, not sanctioned amounts; no new money disbursed)
recommended_products.repayment: amortising EMI with 6-month principal moratorium; post-moratorium monthly principal = INR 171,000,000 / 78 months = INR 2,192,308; interest-only during moratorium at ~INR 1,638,750/month

serviceability_check: EBITDA FY2025-26 (latest year, used conservatively) = INR 50,568,000
Interest on restructured TL: INR 171,000,000 × 11.5% = INR 19,665,000 per annum (full-year; moratorium is principal-only, interest runs from Day 1)
Post-moratorium annual principal repayment: INR 171,000,000 / 78 months × 12 = INR 26,307,692 per annum
Annual debt service on restructured TL = INR 19,665,000 + INR 26,307,692 = INR 45,972,692

Existing WC facilities (CC INR 104 Mn @ 10.2% + WCDL INR 39 Mn @ 11.5%) are revolving — no principal EMI; annual interest = (104,000,000 × 10.2%) + (39,000,000 × 11.5%) = INR 10,608,000 + INR 4,485,000 = INR 15,093,000
Total annual debt service post-restructuring = INR 45,972,692 (new TL) + INR 15,093,000 (WC interest) = INR 61,065,692
Post-restructuring DSCR = INR 50,568,000 / INR 61,065,692 = 0.83x — STILL BELOW 1.25x threshold
DSCR reaches 1.25x only if EBITDA grows to INR 61,065,692 × 1.25 = INR 76,332,115 — requires ~51% EBITDA growth from FY26 base; this is NOT achievable in Year 1

Therefore: restructuring alone is insufficient without (a) promoter equity infusion of INR 15 Mn (reduces interest base) AND (b) EBITDA improvement to at least INR 65 Mn (Year 2 target at ~5% revenue CAGR + margin recovery to ~10%)

Sensitivity — if promoter infuses INR 15 Mn to partially repay highest-cost debt (Aditya Birla @ 12.4%, reduce outstanding to INR 37 Mn): revised TL pool = INR 119 Mn + INR 37 Mn = INR 156 Mn; annual principal = INR 156 Mn / 78 × 12 = INR 24,000,000; interest = INR 156 Mn × 11.5% = INR 17,940,000; total TL service = INR 41,940,000; total service incl. WC = INR 57,033,000; DSCR = INR 50,568,000 / INR 57,033,000 = 0.89x — still below 1.25x in Year 1

CONCLUSION: Restructuring is structurally necessary to prevent default but DSCR will remain below 1.25x in Year 1 even post-restructuring; lender must condition approval on (i) promoter equity infusion, (ii) EBITDA covenant step-up schedule, and (iii) escrow of all collections — this is a distressed restructuring, not a standard credit approval; no new money is disbursed

While 0-60 day eligible receivables of INR 87.9 Mn could theoretically support ~INR 61-75 Mn at 70-85% advance rate, the self-liquidating nature does not address the structural insolvency; 12% of book is 90+ days overdue; top customer is 33% concentrated; and adding any new facility without resolving the INR 44.7 Mn cash reconciliation gap (data-quality flag) would be imprudent

Existing WCDL (Yes Bank INR 39 Mn) is 97.5% utilised; WC cycle gap (DSO 74d + inventory 63d - DPO 52d = 85 days) is already funded beyond capacity; new WCDL adds revolving interest with no improvement in serviceability

Not applicable — company is not pre-revenue or equity-backed in a growth stage; Helios Growth Fund holds only 10%; PAT losses are operational, not investment-phase; venture debt moratorium would defer but not resolve the structural DSCR deficit

key_risks: DSCR 0.57x (critical): restructuring extends tenor to 84 months and adds 6-month moratorium, reducing annual principal outflow; escrow of collections ensures debt service is prioritised over discretionary spend

Negative net worth INR -11.6 Mn (critical): promoter equity infusion of INR 15 Mn is a hard condition precedent; personal guarantees of all three promoters (90% combined) provide recourse beyond corporate balance sheet
Debt/EBITDA 6.21x (high): no new money disbursed; restructuring reduces effective debt service; leverage covenant steps down from 5.0x to 3.0x over 4 years with semi-annual testing

Cash reconciliation gap INR 44.7 Mn (data-quality critical): two conflicting cash figures (BS INR 5.4 Mn vs bank statement INR 50.1 Mn) could indicate undisclosed liabilities or window-dressing; resolution is a hard CP before any disbursement

Missing sanction letters for 3 of 4 facilities: full debt schedule cannot be verified; lender consent for refinancing cannot be obtained without original sanction terms; submission of all four sanction letters is a CP
Customer concentration 33% (medium): concentration covenant capped at 35% with spread step-up on breach; monthly receivables ageing monitoring flags deterioration early
90+ day receivables 12% of book (medium): escrow/collection account routes all debtor payments through lender-monitored account; ageing report triggers if 90+ bucket exceeds 15%
2 cheque bounces in 12 months (medium): cash collateral FD of INR 5 Mn (1-month EMI reserve) provides buffer; bounce confirmation CP ensures these are not debt-service related

Thin liquidity 0.09 months cover (high): escrow structure and moratorium together preserve operating cash during restructuring period; current ratio covenant relaxed to 1.10x initially with step-up to 1.20x by Year 2
rationale: DSCR 0.57x is critically below 1.0x — existing INR 88.75 Mn annual debt service exceeds EBITDA of INR 50.57 Mn; new senior debt is categorically declined.
Negative net worth of INR -11.6 Mn signals technical insolvency; no new lender can take a junior position on this balance sheet without equity cure.
Debt/EBITDA of 6.21x is more than 2x the 3.0x norm; total borrowings of INR 314 Mn against EBITDA of INR 50.57 Mn leave no headroom for incremental debt.
Restructuring consolidates INR 171 Mn of term debt (ICICI TL + AB Finance TL) into 84-month facility; 6-month moratorium reduces near-term cash drain.
Post-restructuring DSCR of 0.83x–0.89x (with equity infusion) still below 1.25x in Year 1 — approval is conditional on EBITDA recovery to ~INR 65 Mn by Year 2 (10.8% margin on projected revenue).
Data-quality flag: INR 44.7 Mn gap between BS cash (INR 5.4 Mn) and bank statement (INR 50.1 Mn) is unresolved; conservative sizing uses BS figure; reconciliation is a hard CP.
Only one of four sanction letters is in the dataroom; full debt schedule verification and lender NOCs are mandatory CPs before restructuring can close.
Promoter equity infusion of INR 15 Mn is a non-negotiable CP — applied to highest-cost debt (AB Finance @ 12.4%) to maximise DSCR improvement per rupee of infusion.
Escrow of all receivable collections through a lender-controlled account is the primary credit mitigant given thin liquidity (0.09 months cover) and near-maxed WC utilisation (95.3%).
Customer concentration at 33% (top customer) is within the 35% covenant threshold but warrants monitoring; breach triggers 50 bps spread step-up to incentivise diversification.
Two cheque bounces in 12 months are medium severity but require confirmation they are not debt-service related; cash collateral FD of INR 5 Mn provides one-month EMI buffer.
No new working-capital facility is recommended; existing CC (INR 110 Mn) and WCDL (INR 40 Mn) are retained as-is — adding WC debt on a 95.3%-utilised, loss-making book would be imprudent.
